title: Spatial Forcing: Implicit Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-language-action Model
claim: Aligning a model's intermediate visual embeddings with a frozen expert's representations adds spatial knowledge, improving efficiency, accuracy and probed perception.
layout: 3 panels: large pipeline left, plot and image strip right; dashed dividers
description: The figure has three panels separated by dashed lines. Panel (a), on the left, is a method diagram. A frozen 3D foundation model and image and text tokenizers feed colored token squares into stacked VLA layers, which sit under an Action output. A dashed arrow from the image tokens at layer i leads to a gray Spatial Forcing Alignment box that connects back to the 3D model's tokens. A flame icon marks the trainable VLA and a snowflake marks the frozen model. A robot scene photo and a text instruction are the inputs. Panel (b), top right, has two rounded cards: a line chart of training efficiency, where w/ SF in blue converges faster than w/o SF in orange, with a 3.8x arrow, and a bar chart of test accuracy for SpatialVLA, π0 and SF. Panel (c), bottom right, is a row of depth maps: input image, w/o SF, w/ SF and ground truth, with orange and blue borders. Blue, orange and green pastel colors carry meaning throughout.
caption: Our proposed method, Spatial Forcing (SF), implicitly forces VLA models to acquire spatial-aware knowledge. (a) SF aligns intermediate visual embeddings of VLAs with geometric representations from pretrained 3D foundation models. (b) Our simple yet effective strategy yields significant improvements in training efficiency and test accuracy. (c) Depth probing proves that our SF brings spatial information into the aligned representations, further enhancing 3D perception.
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have recently shown strong potential in enabling robots to follow language instructions and execute precise actions. However, most VLAs are built upon vision-language models pretrained solely on 2D data, which lack accurate spatial awareness and hinder their ability to operate in the 3D physical world. Existing solutions attempt to incorporate explicit 3D sensor inputs such as depth maps or point clouds, but these approaches face challenges due to sensor noise, hardware heterogeneity, and incomplete depth coverage in existing datasets. Alternative methods that estimate 3D cues from 2D images also suffer from the limited performance of depth estimators. We propose Spatial Forcing (SF), a simple yet effective alignment strategy that implicitly forces VLA models to develop spatial comprehension capabilities without relying on explicit 3D inputs or depth estimators. SF aligns intermediate visual embeddings of VLAs with geometric representations produced by pretrained 3D foundation models. By enforcing alignment at intermediate layers, SF guides VLAs to encode richer spatial representations that enhance action precision. Extensive experiments in simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that SF achieves state-of-the-art results, surpassing both 2D- and 3D-based VLAs. SF further accelerates training by up to 3.8x and improves data efficiency across diverse robotic tasks. Project page is at https://spatial-forcing.github.io/
